subtitle: Mahendralal Sarkar and the Birth of Indian-Run Science

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot, low angle, Sarkar in Victorian Bengali attire before a half-built Calcutta house with scientific instruments faintly visible inside
panels.action: Mahendralal Sarkar stands firm in a Calcutta street, one hand holding rolled plans, behind him an unfinished building that hints at lecture halls and lab benches in shadow.

dialogue.text: In colonial Calcutta, when British funds shut Indians out of science, Mahendralal Sarkar dared to build a research house from public coins and stubborn will.

i18n.hi: औपनिवेशिक कलकत्ता में, जब अंग्रेजी फंड ने हिंदुस्तानियों को विज्ञान से दूर रखा, तब महेंद्रलाल सरकार ने जनता के पैसे और ज़िद से रिसर्च का घर खड़ा करने की ठानी।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot, Sarkar seated at a desk, candlelight on his face, medical diploma and stethoscope nearby
panels.action: In a modest Calcutta chamber, young Dr Mahendralal Sarkar sits at a wooden desk, his Calcutta Medical College diploma on the wall, candlelight catching the worry lines on his brow.

dialogue.text: He was the second MD of Calcutta Medical College, trained in Western medicine, yet each day he saw a harsher lesson: science here wore a foreign badge.

i18n.hi: वो कलकत्ता मेडिकल कॉलेज के दूसरे एमडी थे, पाश्चात्य चिकित्सा के उस्ताद, पर रोज़ एक कड़वा सच देखते थे: यहां की साइंस पर पराए हक़ का तगमा लगा था।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Sarkar’s hand turning pages of a thick English scientific volume
panels.action: Sarkar’s fingers trace diagrams in a heavy English science book; beyond the open window, the bustle of Calcutta’s Indian streets feels far away from the printed world inside.

dialogue.text: The journals, laboratories, learned societies that drove modern science were run by the colonial state and its officers; Indians could study, but seldom decide.

i18n.hi: जर्नल, लैबोरेटरी, वैज्ञानिक सोसायटी—जो आधुनिक विज्ञान को चलाते थे—सब सूबेदारी सरकार और उसके अफ़सरों के हाथ में थे; हिंदुस्तानी पढ़ सकते थे, पर फैसले नहीं कर सकते थे।

panels.shot: wide shot in a European-style hall, British officials at a long table, Sarkar standing at the edge of the room
panels.action: In a grand colonial hall with high arches, British officials in stiff coats confer around a table of reports, while Sarkar stands at the margin, listening yet clearly apart.

dialogue.text: In official scientific bodies, Indians were invited to attend, not to shape policy; decisions on research, funding, and priorities passed over their heads.

i18n.hi: सरकारी वैज्ञानिक संस्थाओं में हिंदुस्तानियों को बुलाया तो जाता था, पर नीति बनाने नहीं; रिसर्च, फंड और तर्ज़ीह के फैसले उनके सिर के ऊपर से गुजर जाते थे।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Sarkar addressing a small group of Indian professionals in a parlour
panels.action: In a Bengali gentleman’s parlour, books lining the walls, Sarkar leans forward as he speaks to a circle of Indian lawyers, teachers and doctors, his eyes intense but hopeful.

dialogue.speaker: mahendralal_sarkar
dialogue.text: If we wait for their invitation, we will wait forever. We must build our own house of science.

i18n.hi: अगर हम उनकी बुलाहट का इंतज़ार करेंगे, तो हमेशा ही करेंगे। हमें अपना विज्ञान का घर खुद बनाना होगा।

panels.shot: close-up of a hand writing the words “Calcutta Journal of Medicine” on a title page
panels.action: A pen scratches across paper, forming the bold title “Calcutta Journal of Medicine” on a fresh issue, with Sarkar seated nearby, revising an article with determined focus.

dialogue.text: From 1868, he turned to print, using the Calcutta Journal of Medicine to argue for medical reform and a wider scientific culture open to Indian minds.

i18n.hi: 1868 से उसने कलम उठाई, ‘कलकत्ता जर्नल ऑफ़ मेडिसिन’ से मेडिकल सुधार और हिंदुस्तानी दिमाग़ों के लिए खुली वैज्ञानिक संस्कृति की वकालत शुरू की।

panels.shot: thoughtful mid-shot, Sarkar with two contrasting books: a homeopathy text and a physiology manual
panels.action: At his desk, Sarkar weighs two volumes in his hands, one a homeopathic text, the other a Western physiology manual, his face calm but marked by inner debate.

dialogue.text: He defended homeopathy while embracing modern medical science, a complex reformer in a Bengal torn by arguments over what counted as ‘true’ medicine.

i18n.hi: उसने होम्योपैथी का बचाव किया, पर आधुनिक चिकित्सा भी अपनाई—बंगाल की उस जंग में एक पेचीदा सुधारक, जहां ‘सच्ची’ दवा पर झगड़े चल रहे थे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Sarkar standing before a map of India pinned to a wall
panels.action: Sarkar stands before a large map of India, pins marking different cities, as if imagining centres of learning across the land; outside, the sounds of the colonial city drift in.

dialogue.text: By 1867 he began to push a sharper idea: a public-funded Indian institution for experimental research and lectures, owned and directed by Indians themselves.

i18n.hi: 1867 तक उसने एक नुकीला ख़याल आगे धकेला: जनता के फंड से चलने वाली देसी प्रयोगशाला और लेक्चर का संस्थान, जिसका मालिक और निर्देशक खुद हिंदुस्तानी हों।

panels.shot: busy street scene, mid-shot of Sarkar speaking to a small crowd of Bengali bhadralok and traders
panels.action: In a crowded Calcutta bazaar street, Sarkar stands on a small step, addressing attentive Bengali gentlemen and traders, their clothes a mix of dhotis, shawls and tailored jackets.

dialogue.text: He carried the idea into drawing rooms and markets, arguing that science must not be a distant spectacle but a shared Indian enterprise, funded by everyday people.

i18n.hi: वो ड्रॉइंग रूम से लेकर बाज़ारों तक बात ले गया—दलील दी कि विज्ञान कोई दूर का तमाशा नहीं, आम हिंदुस्तानियों की साझी मेहनत होना चाहिए, रोज़मर्रा के पैसों से।

panels.shot: close-up of coins and promissory notes dropping into a wooden box
panels.action: Hands of different ages and status place coins and signed pledges into a simple wooden box, while Sarkar watches quietly from the side, notebook in hand.

dialogue.text: Instead of pleading at colonial offices, he opened a subscription list; rupees, annas and promises of support began to collect in a modest box on an Indian table.

i18n.hi: राज के दफ़्तरों में गुहार लगाने की जगह उसने चंदे की सूची खोली; रुपये, आने और मदद के वादे एक सादा हिंदुस्तानी मेज़ पर रखे छोटे से बक्से में जमा होने लगे।

panels.shot: interior mid-shot, Sarkar addressing a committee of Indian leaders around a table
panels.action: Around a long table, a committee of Indian professionals listens as Sarkar stands at the head, pointing to a draft deed on the table, his voice steady but urgent.

dialogue.text: Through meetings and minutes he helped shape a plan: an association to cultivate science with public lectures and research, governed by its members, not the Raj.

i18n.hi: बैठकों और नोटों के ज़रिए उसने एक नक्शा गढ़ने में मदद की: विज्ञान को बढ़ाने वाली ऐसी सोसायटी जो पब्लिक लेक्चर और रिसर्च करे, और जिसके मालिक उसके सदस्य हों, राज नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on the heading of a founding deed being signed, date faintly visible as 29 July 1876
panels.action: A feathered pen signs below printed words on a deed; above, the title ‘Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science’ and the date 29 July 1876 are visible on the parchment.

dialogue.text: On 29 July 1876, the founding deed was signed in Calcutta: the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science, an independent research institution run by Indians.

i18n.hi: 29 जुलाई 1876 को कलकत्ता में बुनियादी दस्तावेज़ पर दस्तखत हुए: इंडियन असोसिएशन फ़ॉर द कल्टिवेशन ऑफ़ साइंस—हिंदुस्तानियों के हाथों चलने वाला आज़ाद रिसर्च संस्थान।

panels.shot: wide exterior shot of the first IACS building, modest but proud, with people entering
panels.action: A simple but dignified building stands on a Calcutta lane, its doorway busy with Indian students and scholars walking in, as Sarkar watches from the side with quiet satisfaction.

dialogue.text: The building was modest, the funds limited, yet it was a new kind of space: an Indian-run house where physics, chemistry and natural science could be pursued for their own sake.

i18n.hi: इमारत मामूली थी, फंड कम थे, पर जगह नई किस्म की थी: देसी लोगों द्वारा चलाया गया ऐसा घर, जहां फिजिक्स, केमिस्ट्री और नेचुरल साइंस सिर्फ़ ज्ञान के लिए की जा सके।

panels.shot: interior wide shot of a lecture hall, Sarkar at a podium addressing an Indian audience
panels.action: Inside the association’s hall, Sarkar stands at a wooden lectern, chalkboard behind him, speaking to rows of Indian listeners as diagrams and apparatus rest on nearby tables.

dialogue.speaker: mahendralal_sarkar
dialogue.text: Let this be a place where the poorest Indian may hear of the stars, the atom, and the laws of nature.

i18n.hi: ये जगह ऐसी हो, जहां सबसे ग़रीब हिंदुस्तानी भी सितारों, अणु और प्रकृति के क़ानूनों की बातें सुन सके।

panels.shot: mid-shot of simple experimental apparatus on a bench, with Sarkar guiding a younger man
panels.action: On a plain wooden bench, basic scientific instruments stand ready; Sarkar leans over, instructing a younger Indian student adjusting a device, both absorbed in the work.

dialogue.text: It was not the richest laboratory in the empire, but it offered something rarer: Indian students learning and experimenting in a place answerable to their own society.

i18n.hi: ये साम्राज्य की सबसे अमीर लैब नहीं थी, पर एक दुर्लभ चीज़ देती थी: हिंदुस्तानी छात्र अपने समाज को जवाबदेह जगह में पढ़ते और खुद प्रयोग करते थे।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite, the building of IACS remaining while British officials change around it
panels.action: In a visual blend, colonial officials in different uniforms fade and change over years, while the IACS building stays steady at the centre, its doorway always open.

dialogue.text: As official policies shifted and governments changed, the association’s deeper claim remained: Indians could imagine, fund and govern serious scientific work themselves.

i18n.hi: नीतियां बदलती रहीं, सरकारें आती-जाती रहीं, पर असोसिएशन का गहरा दावा कायम रहा: गंभीर वैज्ञानिक काम की कल्पना, फंडिंग और हुकूमत हिंदुस्तानी खुद कर सकते हैं।

panels.shot: symbolic shot, empty laboratory with shafts of light on instruments, hinting at future discoveries
panels.action: An empty laboratory room in IACS lies quiet, morning light falling on simple instruments and glassware, suggesting the untapped work that will someday unfold there.

dialogue.text: Decades later, this house would host C.V. Raman’s experiments, but its first victory was simpler: it proved that a research institution could grow from Indian subscriptions and resolve.

i18n.hi: दशकों बाद इसी घर में सी. वी. रामन के प्रयोग हुए, पर इसकी पहली जीत और सरल थी: यह साबित कर देना कि रिसर्च संस्थान हिंदुस्तानी चंदे और हौसले से भी उग सकता है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Sarkar’s thoughtful eyes, older now, looking beyond the frame
panels.action: An older Sarkar gazes out of a window, his eyes reflective, the city’s roofs stretching before him, the sounds of lectures faintly drifting from rooms behind.

dialogue.text: He did not resolve every medical debate he entered, nor was he a laboratory pioneer in every field; his enduring work was institutional, the creation of a space and tradition.

i18n.hi: हर मेडिकल बहस वो जीत नहीं पाया, न हर मैदान में लैब का सरदार बना; उसकी टिकाऊ मेहनत संस्थागत थी—एक जगह और एक रिवायत खड़ी करना।

panels.shot: final wide shot from above, showing IACS nestled within the larger city of Calcutta
panels.action: From high above, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science sits among Calcutta’s mix of colonial buildings and Indian neighbourhoods, a quiet but distinct landmark.

dialogue.text: Mahendralal Sarkar’s science house reminds us that institutions begin when one person refuses to wait for permission, and gathers a community to change what seems fixed.

i18n.hi: महेंद्रलाल सरकार का विज्ञान-घर याद दिलाता है कि संस्थान तब जन्म लेते हैं जब कोई एक इंसान इजाज़त का इंतज़ार करने से मना करता है, और मिलकर जमात खड़ी करता है ताकि जमे-जमाए ढांचे बदल सकें।

title_i18n.en: The Doctor Who Built a Science House
title_i18n.hi: वो डॉक्टर जिसने बनाया विज्ञान का घर

subtitle_i18n.en: Mahendralal Sarkar and the Birth of Indian-Run Science
subtitle_i18n.hi: महेंद्रलाल सरकार और देसी विज्ञान की पैदाइश
